text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Greek Cypriot side will be taking exams for accession into European Union at Amenia, New York, where direct talks are scheduled with Turkish Cypriot side on Cyprus dispute this week. "If we are not held responsible for their possible failure there will be no barrier to accession," says President Clerides.
- Party leaders express pessimism at prospects of coming talks. "There is no indication of a move in Turkish positions," they say.
- United Nations has two plans of action on ways to achieve progress during direct talks in New York.
- Flies suspected of coming from Turkey are destroying citrus crops in Astromeritis-Peristerona region, 35 km (22 miles) northwest of Nicosia.
- Authorities have started snap checks on establishments where cylinder gas is used, to minimise risk of accidents.
- Political leaders not optimistic on outcome of New York talks. Clerides: "We are going to New York with goodwill."
